resources.string: Play music or a video to see its level.
Take breaks and avoid long sessions.
Turn it down! Safe for only about %1$s a day.
Peak this session: %1$d dB (tap to reset)
Red: 85 dB and above – dangerous with long listening
Loudness scale from green to red

Phones can\'t know how loud your speaker or headphones really are, so the number is an estimate (a full-scale signal at full volume is assumed to be 100 dB). If you have a sound-level meter, nudge this until both agree.

Measures what your phone plays (music, videos, games), not the microphone. Android requires the microphone permission to capture audio output, but no microphone audio is recorded or saved, and nothing leaves your phone. Some apps (e.g. DRM-protected video) block capture and will show as silent, and phone calls can\'t be measured. This is a guide, not a medical device.
Too loud! %1$d dB – turn it down
Microphone permission is needed so Android lets this app capture your phone\'s audio output. No microphone audio is recorded.
Screen-capture permission was not granted. Android uses it to allow audio capture; no screen is recorded.
